support_line: Open PayNest, go to Profile > Help & Support, and use the in-app support chat. Do not use phone numbers or links that someone sent you.

entries.answer: This looks like a fake KYC scam. PayNest will never call or message you demanding urgent KYC, and will never ask for your OTP, PIN or password. Do not click any link, install any app or share any code. End the call. If you are worried about your KYC status, open the PayNest app yourself and check it there, or contact support through the in-app Help & Support chat. Banks and payment providers only handle KYC through their official app, website or branch. If money has already been lost, report it immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or the cybercrime helpline 1930, and inform your bank. Confirm these details on the official sites, as they can change.

entries.answer: Act quickly. 1) Change your PayNest PIN and password from inside the app. 2) If you installed an app at someone's request, uninstall it and turn on airplane mode until you have removed it. 3) Contact your bank or card provider if card details were entered. 4) Report the incident through in-app Help & Support so the account can be reviewed. 5) Keep screenshots of messages and the sender's details. Do not delay, since speed matters. If money has already been lost, report it immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or the cybercrime helpline 1930, and inform your bank. Ask the buyer to pay you directly using your own payment ID, and confirm the money actually shows in your Transaction History before handing over anything. If money has already been lost, report it immediately on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or the cybercrime helpline 1930, and inform your bank.
